name: Three-act structure
description: Universal structure of construction, confrontation and resolution.

acts.title: Act 1: Setup
acts.description: Characters, starting point and central conflict are established.

beats.title: Initial situation
beats.description: The previous world and the unfulfilled need become visible.
guidingQuestions: What is normal for the main character?

beats.title: Triggering event
beats.description: An event permanently disrupts the previous order.

beats.title: First turning point
beats.description: The main character chooses the central conflict.

acts.title: Act 2: Confrontation
acts.description: Resistance grows and changes the understanding of the conflict.

beats.title: Rising obstacles
beats.description: Attempts by the main character create more difficult problems.
guidingQuestions: Why isn't the first plan enough?

beats.title: Center point
beats.description: A revelation or reversal changes the goal and stakes.
guidingQuestions: What can no longer be reversed afterwards?

beats.title: crisis
beats.description: The pressure is reaching a point where the current path fails.
guidingQuestions: What does the main character lose?

beats.title: Second turning point
beats.description: A final insight or decision leads to the finale.
guidingQuestions: What makes the last attempt possible?

acts.title: Act 3: Resolution
acts.description: The central conflict is decided and its effects are shown.

beats.title: Final preparation
beats.description: Forces and decisions are gathering for the final confrontation.

beats.title: climax
beats.description: The main character faces the decisive conflict.
guidingQuestions: What decision does the development prove?

beats.title: New normality
beats.description: The consequences of the finale and the changed world become visible.
guidingQuestions: What did the main character gain or lose?
